title: Genuine certification of incompatible quantum instruments through sequential communication tasks
authors: Arindam Mitra, Satyaki Manna, Debashis Saha
abstract: Quantum instruments constitute the general description of quantum dynamics, encompassing both quantum measurements and quantum channels as special cases. Consequently, the incompatibility of quantum instruments represents a fundamental manifestation of nonclassicality in quantum theory. Here, we establish the operational significance of this notion by demonstrating communication tasks with classical inputs and outputs that enable the semi-device-independent certification of incompatible quantum instruments. We introduce a class of three-party communication tasks involving a sender, a relayer, and a receiver, and derive the tight upper bound of the figure of merits of these tasks achievable by all compatible instruments implemented by the relayer and this bound coincides with the optimal performance attainable in a classical communication subject to the same dimensional constraints. Violation of this bound certifies the incompatibility of the pair of quantum instruments implemented by the relayer. This identifies certification of incompatible instruments as a manifestation of quantum advantage in communication. This certification protocol is genuine as it is able to certify the incompatibility of a pair of instruments where the measurements and channels induced by the instruments are pairwise compatible and, therefore it does not depend on the incompability of measurements and channels induced by the instruments. Finally, we identify the simplest instances of our communication scenario that enable the certification of incompatible quantum instruments.
summary: The paper introduces a novel method to certify that two quantum instruments are incompatible by designing a specific three-party sequential communication task. By showing that the maximum achievable performance in this task exceeds the classical limit, they prove the nonclassical nature (incompatibility) of the instruments. This establishes instrument incompatibility as an operational resource for quantum advantage.
main_problem: To establish an operational method for certifying the incompatibility of quantum instruments, which is a fundamental manifestation of nonclassicality in quantum theory.
main_result: The authors developed a genuine certification protocol using sequential communication tasks where violating a classical bound proves that the implemented quantum instruments are incompatible. This demonstrates instrument incompatibility as a source of quantum advantage in communication.
method: They analyze a three-party sequential communication task, comparing the achievable 'figure of merit' for quantum vs. classically constrained strategies to derive necessary bounds for compatibility.
model_or_system: The model involves three parties (sender, relayer, receiver) and focuses on quantum instruments, which generalize measurements and channels. The core diagnostic tool is a figure of merit derived from conditional probabilities in the communication task.
key_observables: Figure of merit ($S$), comparing $S_{Q}^{	ext{op}}$ (quantum optimum), $S_{QC}^{	ext{op}}$ (compatible quantum optimum), and $S_{C}^{	ext{op}}$ (classical optimum).
important_parameters: The task is generalized using $(m_A, d)$-sequential XOR tasks; specific results are derived for the $(2, 2)$ case.
main_assumptions: The protocol's genuineness relies on it not depending on the pairwise compatibility of induced measurements and channels, even when instruments themselves might be intrinsically incompatible.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general setup for instrument incompatibility certification using sequential communication tasks, showing special cases for measurement and channel incompatibility.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the problem using a three-party task. It then establishes bounds by comparing quantum vs. classical performance (Propositions 1 & 2). The core results are presented via analyzing specific XOR tasks ($(m_A, d)$-tasks), proving quantum advantage ($	ext{SQ} > 	ext{SC}$) for incompatible instruments.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general framework to detect fundamental nonclassical features (like instrument incompatibility) using communication protocols, which is highly relevant for understanding the limits of quantum information processing.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Fig. (a) depicts the scenario of instrument incompatibility certification that we explore in this work. The scenarios depicted Fig. (b) and Fig. (c) are the scenarios of measurement and channel incompatibility certification scenarios respectively and are the special cases of the scenario depicted in Fig. (a) which is unified.

FIG. 2. The instrument J0 induces a channel Ψ0 and a measurement M0. Similarly, the instrument J1 induces channel Ψ1 and measurement M1. All induced measurements and channels are pairwise compatible. But Jo and J1 are incompatible. Therefore, any certification protocol that is able to certify the incompatibility of J0 and J1, does not depend on the incompatibility of induced measurements and channels and therefore, it is genuine.
